exposure: A combined infection prevention and control (IPC) with antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) joint program (including formal and on-job IPC trainings, and evidence-based education on antimicrobial resistance and good antimicrobial prescribing practice)
outcome: Post-caesarean section surgical site infections prevalence
Determinant factors of surgical site infections
Microbiological characteristics and patterns of antimicrobial resistance
cohort: The study included 464 women surveyed before and 573 women surveyed after the intervention, all undergoing caesarean sections at a Tanzanian tertiary hospital.
finding: The combined IPC and AMS joint program significantly reduced the prevalence of post-caesarean section surgical site infections from 48% before the intervention to 17% after the intervention (p < 0.001).
mod_finding: The intervention was specifically designed and found to be effective in reducing surgical site infections following caesarean sections.
cross-section timing: Surveys were conducted before the implementation of the combined IPC and AMS program and again after its implementation.
